text: When Jesus had said all this, he went out with his disciples across the Kidron Valley, where there was a garden, and he and his disciples went into it.
Judas, who was betraying him, also knew the place, because Jesus had often met there with his disciples.
So Judas came there with a detachment of soldiers and with officers from the chief priests and the Pharisees, carrying lanterns, torches, and weapons.
Jesus, knowing everything that was coming upon him, went out and asked them, "Who are you looking for?"
"Jesus of Nazareth," they answered. Jesus said to them, "I am he." Judas, who was betraying him, was standing there with them.
When he said, "I am he," they drew back and fell to the ground.
So he asked them again, "Who are you looking for?" And they said, "Jesus of Nazareth."
Jesus answered, "I told you that I am he. So if you are looking for me, let these men go."
This was to fulfill the word he had spoken: "Of those you gave me, I have not lost one."
Then Simon Peter, who had a sword, drew it and struck the high priest's servant, cutting off his right ear. The servant's name was Malchus.
So Jesus said to Peter, "Put your sword back in its sheath. Shall I not drink the cup the Father has given me?"
Then the detachment of soldiers with its commander and the Jewish officers arrested Jesus and bound him.
They brought him first to Annas, who was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, the high priest that year.
Caiaphas was the one who had advised the Jews that it was better for one man to die for the people.
Simon Peter and another disciple were following Jesus. Since that disciple was known to the high priest, he went with Jesus into the high priest's courtyard,
but Peter stood outside at the door. So the other disciple, who was known to the high priest, went out and spoke to the woman at the door, and brought Peter in.

versions.text: but Peter stood outside at the door. So the other disciple, who was known to the high priest, went out and spoke to the woman keeping the door, and brought Peter in.
versions.explanation: "The woman keeping the door" is clumsy when read aloud and creates a stumbling cluster of participles; the simpler phrase preserves the sense of θυρωρός while flowing better, and verse 17 makes her role clear.

text: The servant girl at the door said to Peter, "You aren't one of this man's disciples too, are you?" "I am not," he said.
The servants and officers were standing there, warming themselves at a charcoal fire they had made, because it was cold. Peter was standing with them, warming himself as well.
Then the high priest questioned Jesus about his disciples and his teaching.
Jesus answered him, "I have spoken openly to the world. I always taught in synagogues and in the temple, where all the Jews come together. I said nothing in secret.
Why do you question me? Question those who heard what I said to them. Look, these men know what I said.

versions.text: Why do you question me? Question those who heard me. They know what I said."
versions.explanation: Two elements of the Greek are dropped: τί ἐλάλησα αὐτοῖς ("what I spoke to them") is reduced to "heard me," and the emphatic ἴδε ("look"/"behold") is omitted. Restoring them keeps the full sense and the rhetorical force for oral reading.

versions.text: Why do you question me? Question those who heard what I said to them. Look, they know what I said.
versions.explanation: The demonstrative οὗτοι is emphatic and points to the actual hearers present in the situation; rendering it as "these men" (rather than the unstressed "they") preserves the force of Jesus' gesture toward his audience and clarifies the pronoun's reference for a listener. The current reading is a legitimate rendering, just less pointed.

text: When he said this, one of the officers standing nearby struck Jesus in the face and said, "Is that how you answer the high priest?"
Jesus replied, "If I said something wrong, testify to what was wrong. But if I spoke rightly, why do you strike me?"
Then Annas sent him, still bound, to Caiaphas the high priest.
Meanwhile Simon Peter was standing there warming himself. They said to him, "You aren't one of his disciples too, are you?" He denied it and said, "I am not."
One of the high priest's servants, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, said, "Didn't I see you in the garden with him?"
Again Peter denied it, and at once a rooster crowed.

Then they took Jesus from Caiaphas to the governor's headquarters. It was early morning, and they did not enter the headquarters themselves, so that they would not be defiled but could eat the Passover.
So Pilate came out to them and said, "What charge do you bring against this man?"
They answered, "If he were not a criminal, we would not have handed him over to you."
Pilate said to them, "Take him yourselves and judge him by your own law." The Jews answered, "We are not permitted to put anyone to death."
This was to fulfill the word Jesus had spoken, indicating the kind of death he was going to die.
So Pilate went back inside the headquarters, summoned Jesus, and asked him, "Are you the king of the Jews?"
Jesus answered, "Is that your own question, or did others tell you about me?"
"Am I a Jew?" Pilate replied. "Your own nation and the chief priests handed you over to me. What have you done?"

versions.text: "Am I a Jew?" Pilate replied. "Your own nation and its chief priests handed you over to me. What have you done?"
versions.explanation: The Greek has the article with ἀρχιερεῖς ("the chief priests"), not a possessive tied to the nation. "Its chief priests" adds a relationship not in the text.

text: Jesus answered, "My kingdom is not of this world. If my kingdom were of this world, my servants would be fighting to keep me from being handed over to the Jews. But as it is, my kingdom is not from here."

"So you are a king?" Pilate said. Jesus answered, "You say that I am a king. For this I was born, and for this I came into the world: to testify to the truth. Everyone who belongs to the truth listens to my voice."
"What is truth?" Pilate said. With that he went back out to the Jews and told them, "I find no basis for a charge against him.
But it is your custom that I release one prisoner to you at the Passover. So do you want me to release to you the king of the Jews?"
They shouted again, "Not this man, but Barabbas!" Now Barabbas was a bandit.

versions.text: They shouted back, "Not this man, but Barabbas!" Now Barabbas was a rebel.
versions.explanation: πάλιν means "again," which "shouted back" only loosely conveys. Also λῃστής normally denotes a robber or bandit (often an insurrectionist brigand); "bandit" is closer to the Greek, with the political overtone left available rather than asserted.
